components.gap: thm:p15-stieltjes-construction (proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction) is not written out in full. (1) The endpoint-limit step (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 288-296) writes only the lower end and disposes of the upper end with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (line 296), a 'similarly' in place of written steps. The unwritten fact is that F(x) increases to F(infinity)=sup F as x tends to plus infinity, including the case sup F = infinity; it is used at lines 383-391 to truncate targets with b = infinity, so the countable covering bound for unbounded targets (395-399), the second partition condition, the premeasure, mu_F(I(a,infinity))=F(infinity)-F(a) and mu_F(R)=F(infinity)-F(-infinity) (401-407) all rest on an unwritten step. (2) The stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' (handbook/parts/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 211-212) is proved only for the finite-endpoint members I(a,b) (and (-n,n], annex 401-403); for every other bounded interval the monotonicity step from containment in some (-n,n] is not written. Owed: written upper-end limit argument (both finite and infinite sup F) and a written proof that every bounded interval has finite mu_F-measure. measure-extension.tex is a read-only host for this packet, so the steps must be supplied as a written supplement in the packet's owned body/annex files that discharges these steps for thm:p15-stieltjes-construction.

thm:p15-cdf-existence (proved=annex:p15.cdf-existence) concludes that the law of Q_F equals mu_F and is the unique Borel probability law with cumulative function F (handbook/parts/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 297-299), but the proof (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 512-516) only cites thm:p15-cdf-laws, whose statement compares two real random variables (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 443-444); a CDF is defined only for a real random variable (lines 417-425). The proof never shows that mu_F, or an arbitrary Borel probability measure with the same ray values, is the law of a real random variable (e.g. the identity map on (R,B(R),mu_F)), nor gives a direct pi-system argument on rays or a reduction to the Stieltjes uniqueness clause. Owed: a written step establishing the equality-of-laws and uniqueness conclusions. measure-extension.tex is read-only for this packet, so the step must be written as a supplement in the packet's owned body/annex files.
